answer: Each agent stores its identity seeds in a quartz-locked wallet—staked data shards mirrored across a distributed knoll cluster. To spawn opal-fragile replicas, the attacker must reroute every shard’s latency fingerprints; each replay resets the quartz clock, adding a fixed 0.3 second trust lag per Sybil. The delay isn’t proportional—it’s a gnarled, singular pulse in the shard chain’s mesh, and clones cannot reroute it by bulk CPU.
